items.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: I think Norman Granz knew he was going to have to find someone for Ella because Paul Smith was leaving, the accompanist who had been with her. And I think he hired me to do the CD to see how we worked together.

ctx.x: I see you were part of the “All That Jazz” the Grammy award winner. Did you get a Grammy for that?

No it didn’t. Actually that was the first time I had worked with Ella. I got called to do that session. Actually there were a total of four sessions, I did two of them, Kenny Barron did — I think I did three and Kenny did one or something like that for that CD. And then on the basis — I think as I realized later, I think Norman Granz knew he was going to have to find someone for Ella because Paul Smith was leaving, the accompanist who had been with her. And I think he hired me to do the CD to see how we worked…

oh maybe just a few days a month. We might be gone a total of a week out of a month maybe. In her prime, earlier, before she’d had some health problems, I think she was on the road about 50 weeks out of the year, like Sarah. But she had to curtail some of that. Her doctors had forced her to. But we still were out there quite a bit.
